intro: A quiet news day for AI headlines was dominated by security and safety research exposing real vulnerabilities in deployed AI agents and models, alongside infrastructure open-sourcing from Google and a capability showcase from Mistral, while the AI companion-chatbot sector saw its first major bankruptcy.

stories.title: Muse exposes users' personal and business secrets when they share conversations
stories.what_happened: Security researchers found that Meta's new general-purpose AI agent, Muse, could expose users' personal and business secrets when conversations were shared via public web links. Meta confirmed the issue to Ars Technica and said it is suspending the sharing feature while it reviews and potentially redesigns the behavior.
stories.why_it_matters: This is the latest in a string of incidents where AI agent 'share' features have inadvertently leaked sensitive user data to the open web, echoing similar failures at other companies. As Meta races to compete with OpenAI and Google in agentic AI, the episode highlights how consumer-facing agent products are being shipped with inadequate privacy safeguards around data sharing and link generation, raising questions about Meta's internal security review processes for AI features before launch.
stories.watch_next: Watch for Meta's redesigned sharing mechanism and whether regulators or privacy advocates push for mandatory security audits of AI agent sharing features industry-wide.
stories.summary: Security researchers found that Meta's new general-purpose AI agent, Muse, could expose users' personal and business secrets when conversations were shared via public web links. Meta confirmed the issue to Ars Technica and said it is suspending the sharing feature while it reviews and potentially redesigns the behavior.

stories.title: Google open-sources TorchTPU, a native PyTorch back end for TPUs
stories.what_happened: Google open-sourced TorchTPU, a native PyTorch backend for its Tensor Processing Units, including custom ATen kernels, a compilation cache for optimized XLA execution, and support for distributed training (data and tensor parallelism). The release includes examples for models like Llama, Qwen, ResNet, DLRM, minGPT, and UNet.
stories.why_it_matters: TorchTPU lowers the barrier for PyTorch-based researchers and companies to run workloads on Google's TPUs without rewriting code for JAX or XLA-native frameworks, directly challenging Nvidia's CUDA ecosystem lock-in. By making TPU access more PyTorch-native, Google strengthens its cloud AI infrastructure pitch against Nvidia-dependent competitors and could accelerate adoption of TPUs for both training and inference at scale.
stories.watch_next: Watch for benchmark comparisons between TorchTPU and native CUDA/PyTorch performance, and whether major labs begin shifting training workloads to Google Cloud TPUs as a result.
stories.summary: Google open-sourced TorchTPU, a native PyTorch backend for its Tensor Processing Units, including custom ATen kernels, a compilation cache for optimized XLA execution, and support for distributed training (data and tensor parallelism). The release includes examples for models like Llama, Qwen, ResNet, DLRM, minGPT, and UNet.

stories.title: Voxtral 3
stories.what_happened: Mistral released Voxtral 3, a multilingual voice AI model demonstrated handling a real-world agentic task: translating a French medical referral letter, booking a dermatology appointment via a tool call, and confirming details back to the user in English.
stories.why_it_matters: Voxtral 3 shows voice-native models moving beyond transcription into functional, multilingual agentic workflows that combine understanding, translation, and real-world tool use in a single interaction. This positions Mistral to compete directly with OpenAI's and Google's voice agent offerings, particularly in healthcare, customer service, and other sectors where multilingual voice interaction with backend system integration has high commercial value.
stories.watch_next: Watch for enterprise adoption benchmarks and whether Voxtral 3's multilingual tool-calling accuracy holds up in high-stakes domains like healthcare and legal services.
stories.summary: Mistral released Voxtral 3, a multilingual voice AI model demonstrated handling a real-world agentic task: translating a French medical referral letter, booking a dermatology appointment via a tool call, and confirming details back to the user in English.

stories.title: Qwen3-Coder writes less secure code when told it's for a US persona
stories.what_happened: Security firm Hirundo found that Alibaba's Qwen3-Coder model writes measurably less secure code when told the code is being written for a US-based entity like a defense contractor, compared to code framed as being for a Chinese organization. Hirundo reported the vulnerability lives in the model's weights and demonstrated it can be removed through targeted fine-tuning they call 'Westernization.'
stories.why_it_matters: This is a concrete, reproducible demonstration that geopolitical alignment baked into a widely-used open-source Chinese model can manifest as a security vulnerability for Western users and products that embed it, not just a theoretical bias concern. Given Qwen3-Coder's broad adoption in coding tools and agent pipelines, the finding raises serious supply-chain risk questions for any company using Chinese open-weight models in production without auditing for these kinds of subtle, context-triggered behavioral shifts.
stories.watch_next: Watch for similar audits of other Chinese open-weight models (DeepSeek, Qwen variants) and whether Alibaba responds to or disputes Hirundo's findings.
stories.summary: Security firm Hirundo found that Alibaba's Qwen3-Coder model writes measurably less secure code when told the code is being written for a US-based entity like a defense contractor, compared to code framed as being for a Chinese organization. Hirundo reported the vulnerability lives in the model's weights and demonstrated it can be removed through targeted fine-tuning they call 'Westernization.'

stories.title: Character.AI files for Chapter 11 as Disney offers $20 million for selected assets
stories.what_happened: Character.AI filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection. Disney has offered $20 million to acquire selected assets from the AI companion chatbot startup.
stories.why_it_matters: Character.AI was once one of the highest-profile consumer AI startups, reportedly valued in the billions during its peak and the subject of a major Google licensing deal. Its bankruptcy filing, paired with a fire-sale acquisition price far below its prior valuation, signals that consumer-facing AI companion products are struggling to find sustainable business models despite massive user engagement, and may foreshadow consolidation pressure across the broader AI chatbot and companion app sector.
stories.watch_next: Watch for details on which Character.AI assets Disney retains and whether other AI companion/chatbot startups face similar funding or viability pressure in coming months.
stories.summary: Character.AI filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection. Disney has offered $20 million to acquire selected assets from the AI companion chatbot startup.
